text: Minerals are a small part of the diet by volume but cattle need many of them for maintenance, growth, and reproduction: 7 macro-minerals (calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, sodium, potassium, chlorine, sulfur) and 18 trace elements (iron, copper, cobalt, zinc, iodine, manganese, selenium, and others). Soil and plant mineral content directly affects cattle mineral status; deficiency signs include hair discoloration and reproductive problems. Providing a mineral block for cattle to lick daily is a practical way to meet these needs. Vitamin A is the most important vitamin for cattle, essential for growth, reproduction, skin maintenance, and bone development — high-quality forage and leaves supply enough, but straw does not; B-group vitamins are synthesized by the rumen itself.
